question: How many national projects were launched on Wildlife Week 2025 with the theme “Human–Wildlife Coexistence”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Five.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav launched five new national projects during Wildlife Week 2025 under the theme "Human–Wildlife Coexistence" in Dehradun.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The theme for Wildlife Week 2025 was "Human–Wildlife Coexistence," aiming to foster better management of human-wildlife conflicts.**
 
• **Five national conservation projects were launched, including Project Dolphin (Phase II), Project Sloth Bear, and Project Gharial.**
 
• **The event took place at IGNFA, Dehradun, and was organized by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), in collaboration with institutions like the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), ICFRE, IGNFA, and FRI.**
 
• **In addition to the launch, new estimation and monitoring programs were introduced for species like River Dolphins, Tigers, and Snow Leopards.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Project Dolphin (Phase II)__

 __
 
• Part of India's effort to conserve and protect the endangered species of dolphins, particularly in the rivers of India.
 
 
 
• Project Sloth Bear__
 __
 
• Aimed at conservation of sloth bears and their habitats across India, focusing on research, management, and awareness.
 
 
 
• Project Gharial__
 __
 
• A conservation initiative targeting the gharial species, one of the most critically endangered reptiles in India.
 
 
 
• National Hackathon on Human–Wildlife Conflict Coexistence__
 
 
• A standout feature of the event focusing on innovative solutions to mitigate conflicts between humans and wildlife.
